It doesn't guard against a missing scriptloader with `.get(...)` returning None. This is harmless because the scriptloader is always registered by default.
grade.reason: The agent changed the same place as the upstream patch, in main.py before the options dump. It loads all pending scripts so their options are registered. Its `load_if_changed` loads a script only when the mtime is newer than the initial 0.0, which matches upstream's `ns is None` check for scripts that haven't loaded yet. Storing `last_mtime` on the instance stops the watcher from reloading the script afterwards. The refactor is larger than upstream's, but it behaves the same.

result:
`--options` now includes options that addon scripts register. I haven't run the tests or the CLI, and I didn't add a test.

Scripts loaded with `-s` don't load immediately. Each one has a watcher task that defers its first load, so a script's options didn't exist yet when `--options` dumped them.

**`mitmproxy/addons/script.py`**
- The watcher's per-iteration logic is now a `Script.load_if_changed()` method. It loads the script if it is new or modified, and returns `False` if the file has disappeared, in which case it also removes the script from the options.
- The last-seen mtime moved from a local variable in `watcher()` to a `Script.last_mtime` attribute. This means a script loaded early isn't loaded a second time when its watcher wakes up.
- New `ScriptLoader.load_pending()` calls `load_if_changed()` on every script the loader is managing.

**`mitmproxy/tools/main.py`**
- When `args.options` is set, `master.addons.get("scriptloader").load_pending()` runs just before `optmanager.dump_defaults(...)`.

I assumed `ctx.master` is already set when `main()` reaches that point, since `loadscript()` needs it. I haven't confirmed it.

I didn't add a test because `main.run` is marked `# pragma: no cover`. A test for `load_pending` in `test/mitmproxy/addons/test_script.py` would be a natural addition.
